title: PROTOCOL_v2 - Confirmatory test on an untouched set: does kick targeting need learning?
external_timestamp: OSF upload by the author before the first holdout2 run (URL recorded in PROTOCOL_DEVIATIONS.log)
relation_to_PROTOCOL_v1: PROTOCOL.json (2026-11-15) governed the primary campaign; this protocol is a new, separate confirmatory study on a disjoint instance set. All choices below were made on development sets only (vlsi_old, synth_1000, vlsi_primary); holdout2 has never been run.
claim_under_test: Kick targeting improves a fast ILS over uniform kicks; a training-free O(1) geometric proxy is not inferior to learned scorers (GNN, gain-trained MLP); in-run online learning of the scorer hurts.
engine: unchanged fast_ils.py (2-opt + Or-opt, 10-NN candidates, don't-look bits, better-only acceptance, global double-bridge kicks)
machine: Intel Core i5-9300H (4 cores / 8 threads), Windows 11 x64, Python 3.13, numba; 4 worker processes (one per physical core); all strategies of an (instance, seed) run sequentially in the same worker, paired

holdout_set.composition: 6 Waterloo VLSI (bgd4396, frv4410, bgf4475, fqm5087, bnd7168, ida8197), 3 National (eg7146, ar9152, gr9882), 3 TSPLIB (pcb3038, fl3795, fnl4461; used in Phase 1 but in no v2 development run), 42 synthetic (14 uniform, 14 clustered, 14 mixed; n 1500-4000)
holdout_set.reference: published optimum (real instances) / LKH-3 default parameters, 60 s (synthetic)

strategy_definitions.knn_global@0.04:0.75: pool = m = max(12, int(0.04 n)) tour edges with the worst mutual 24-NN rank; each cut w.p. 0.75 on a pool edge
strategy_definitions.excess_global@0.06:0.5: training-free excess-length proxy d(u,v) - (dref(u)+dref(v))/2, dref = mean distance to the 1st and 2nd nearest neighbour; m = max(12, int(0.06 n)); prob 0.5
strategy_definitions.gnn_global@0.04:0.5: frozen LKH-trained GNN (models/gnn_trained.npz), m lowest-probability edges; m = max(12, int(0.04 n)); prob 0.5
strategy_definitions.linprior_global: static linear gain prior (models/online_prior.npz), no learning, default rule
strategy_definitions.onlinewarm_global: same linear model warm-started from the prior, updated online by Thompson-sampling ridge regression on the signed per-kick reward (online_targeting.py: lam 50, nu 0.5, refresh 2000 kicks), default rule

pool_rule_tuning: grid {0.02,0.04,0.06,0.10} x {0.5,0.75,0.9} for knn / excess / gnn on vlsi_primary + synth_1000 (3 seeds, 10 s; tags dev_grid_*). Selection rule written before the grid results: minimise the equal-weight mean over both sets of the per-instance mean gap; keep 0.06/0.75 if within 0.01 pt of the best. None of the chosen rules differed significantly from the default on the development sets (Wilcoxon p >= 0.36); rules with fraction 0.02 were clearly worse. Untuned signals use the default rule.
seed_scheme: start tour seed 7919*(seed+1)+n, identical for all strategies; kick RNG seed 104729+1009*seed (common random numbers); strategy order rotated by seed
metric: gap (%) to the reference at 10 s; mean over the 10 seeds within an instance; the instance is the unit of inference (n = 54)
multiplicity: fixed-sequence (hierarchical) testing in the listed order: a hypothesis is tested at alpha = 0.05 only if every earlier one was rejected; this controls the family-wise error rate. Hypotheses not reached are reported as 'not tested'.

confirmatory_hypotheses.statement: online learning hurts: the online-updated scorer is worse than the same scorer kept static (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank; success = p < 0.05 and mean(a-b) > 0)
targeting with the training-free proxy beats uniform kicks (two-sided Wilcoxon; success = p < 0.05 and mean(a-b) < 0)
the training-free proxy is not inferior to the GNN by more than 0.05 gap points (one-sided Wilcoxon of d - 0.05 < 0)
the training-free proxy is not inferior to the gain-trained MLP by more than 0.05 gap points (one-sided Wilcoxon of d - 0.05 < 0)

margin_justification: 0.05 gap points at 10 s is below the smallest targeting effect observed on development sets (knn/excess vs random, about 0.07); the earlier +-0.025 margin was infeasible at n = 54 (per-instance sd of differences 0.09-0.13 with 5 seeds).
power: development sd of per-instance differences: excess-knn 0.131, gnn-knn 0.091 (5 seeds). With 10 seeds and n = 54, SE about 0.012-0.018; V1 (development effect +0.13 to +0.21) and V2 (-0.07) have > 80% power; V3/V4 have > 80% power if the true difference is <= 0.
secondary_exploratory: knn vs random, excess vs knn, gnn vs knn, gain vs cheap, excess vs gnn superiority (two-sided Wilcoxon, Holm within this family, labelled exploratory)
per-stratum results (real vs synthetic; VLSI / National / TSPLIB / uniform / clustered / mixed)
exclusions: none; crashes or invalid tours are reported, not dropped; an instance with a missing strategy run is re-run, never dropped
deviations: any deviation is appended to PROTOCOL_DEVIATIONS.log with a timestamp before the affected analysis
